t: Paraguay broke from Spanish rule and from Buenos Aires in 1811 and was isolated for decades under the dictator José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia.
The War of the Triple Alliance of 1864–1870 against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay killed a large share of its people, by some estimates over half.
It won the Chaco War against Bolivia in 1932–1935, lived under Stroessner from 1954 to 1989 and has been a democracy since the constitution of 1992.
dyk: Paraguay’s Presidente Hayes department and the town of Villa Hayes are named after the US president Rutherford B. Hayes, whose arbitration award of 1878 gave Paraguay the disputed Chaco.
ev: Paraguay defeats Belgrano’s army and ends the Spanish governor’s authority
José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia becomes supreme dictator
A congress formally declares Paraguay’s independence
The War of the Triple Alliance against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay
Paraguay defeats Bolivia in the Chaco War
Alfredo Stroessner seizes power and rules until 1989
The Itaipú dam, shared with Brazil, begins generating power
A democratic constitution makes Guaraní an official language
